$comment: Declared data dependencies. Rule: no consumer may depend on a field belonging to another index unless that dependency is declared here and checked. Coupling is not the problem — SILENT coupling is. The search.json -> counts -> empty-state relationship is legitimate and load-bearing; what was wrong with it was that nothing said so, and splitting the index would have broken a sentence in a UI with no test failing. checks.py asserts every declared field exists, and refuses a consumer that fetches an index it has not declared.

/api/search.json.counts.cities: printed by the empty state — this is the coupling point. If the index is ever split into search.json + counts.json, this line is what must force the consumer and its contract to be updated rather than silently falling back to a stale hard-coded number.
/api/search.json.kindPlural: the plural of every kind the index emits, so the results headings are not pluralised by adding an s in the browser — five of the twelve kinds do not take one, and the page read "Citys" and "Countrys". A grammar rule guessed in a script is checked by nothing, which is the same argument as counts.cities above.

/api/atlas.json.cities: every destination it can route through
/api/atlas.json.journeys: the curated routes it compares against
/api/atlas.json.journeys.url: where that journey lives, so the browser never composes one. The recommendation band writes a link per journey and the first version built "/journeys/" + slug, which is a second implementation of a route in the one place `c_script_links` cannot resolve — it reads every href a script can write and checks it against the built site, and a concatenated path is precisely what it cannot check. `routes.hash` exists so a URL cannot move without somebody deciding to; one composed in a script moves without anybody deciding anything. Same shape as cities.url.
/api/atlas.json.interests: matching a stated interest to a destination
/api/atlas.json.cities.x: where a destination sits on this atlas's conformal conic, projected at build time. The planner draws the route it built and never moves its frame, so it is handed the answer rather than re-deriving the projection: map.js already has a second implementation because it re-frames continuously, and a third is a third one that drifts.
/api/atlas.json.cities.y: the other half of the same point; see cities.x.
/api/atlas.json.?cities.shot: the URL of one derivative of the photograph the register holds for this destination, for the leg tile. 63 of the 313 rows carry it and the key is ABSENT on the rest, because present-but-empty says “we have this” and then does not. Written by render.photo_href from a register KEY, never from a URL, which is what keeps this from becoming a second way into the library with none of the licence gate behind it — and the reason it crosses a boundary at all is that the planner chooses its stops in the reader's browser, so a build-time set of named stop pictures would be a fake result. DECLARED CONDITIONAL with a leading ?: the key is omitted on the 250 rows the register holds no photograph for, so whether it is “there” depends on which row a checker reads first and it is on no row at all when the register is empty. The assertion is at the producer's source instead.
/api/atlas.json.?cities.shotAlt: the photographer's own description of that photograph, for the alt. Never written here: the alternative to a real one is describing a photograph nothing in this repository has looked at. DECLARED CONDITIONAL with a leading ?: the key is omitted on the 250 rows the register holds no photograph for, so whether it is “there” depends on which row a checker reads first and it is on no row at all when the register is empty. The assertion is at the producer's source instead.
/api/atlas.json.?cities.shotCredit: the attribution Pexels' terms require, as a pre-escaped HTML fragment composed by render.credit_html — the one function that knows the rule. It is carried rather than recomposed in the browser because checks.py's guard against a published page referencing an unregistered file cannot see an a script writes at runtime, so a second implementation of this rule would fail silently and the breach would be of somebody else's terms. If this key disappears the leg photograph must go with it. DECLARED CONDITIONAL with a leading ?: the key is omitted on the 250 rows the register holds no photograph for, so whether it is “there” depends on which row a checker reads first and it is on no row at all when the register is empty. The assertion is at the producer's source instead.

/api/atlas.json.cities: the set Discover Mode narrows. `city.id` is also the join to the map: the build writes it on every dot as `data-city`, and a renamed id would leave the drawing lighting nothing with no error anywhere
resolving saved ids into places, and computing Travel DNA
/api/atlas.json.cities.x: the projected x of a destination, for drawing a saved place on the shared silhouette. It is the SAME number every map on this site is made of, so a saved dot lands where /map puts it and there is no second projection to keep in step
/api/atlas.json.cities.y: the projected y, for the same reason

/api/geo/europe-lod1.json.countries: the finer continent outline, fetched when zoom passes 1.6x
/api/geo/europe-lod1.json.nogeometry: the countries too small to draw at that scale

/api/geo/country/*.json.countries: one country's own level of detail, fetched when it is opened

published_only.$comment: Endpoints with no in-page consumer. They exist because the data is public and the documents are cheap. A shape change here breaks nobody inside this repository, which is exactly why the contract has to be written down: the consumers are people we cannot see.
